newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's scandal taited ex-railway boss set free.
newsitem.headline: Italy's scandal taited ex-railway boss set free.

text.p: The former chief of Italy's state railway company, who was arrested two months ago in a corruption probe, was set free on Wednesday.

Lorenzo Necci, 55, was arrested on September 15 on the orders of magistrates investigating an alleged corrupt "super lobby" to fix jobs in state industries and the judiciary. He was released into house arrest three weeks ago.
The judge who agreed to release Lorenzo Necci from house arrest did not immediately give the reasons for her decision.
"It's downhill from here," said Paolo Balducci, one of Necci's lawyers. "It's a great step forward...from today we will be working to prove that the accusations are unfounded."
Necci has been held on suspicion of committing a raft of corruption-related offences and resigned as managing director of the state railway after his arrest. He has denied wrongdoing.
The affair has mushroomed to include judges, businessmen and lawyers as magistrates probe allegations of trial-fixing, illegal arms exports and widespread bribes for state contracts.

Antonio Di Pietro resigned as public works minister last week after he came under investigation for alleged malpractice during his time as a graft-busting magistrate with Milan's elite 'Clean Hands' pool of prosecutors.

The allegations, which he hotly denies, surfaced during the current scandals, which newspapers have dubbed "Tangentopoli 2", an echo of the "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) corruption scandal which exploded in 1992 and buried Italy's governing elite.
